title: Counting Objects to 20
short: Count up to 20 things in a line, a rectangle or a circle.
trouble: When objects are in a circle, children lose track of where they started and count some twice.

blocks.html: You can read and write numbers to 10 and you know one more. Now count bigger groups, all the way to 20. Things might be in a line, in rows, or in a circle.

blocks.name: k-pic
blocks.cap: Tap one duck to start. Go around once. Stop when you get back to the first one.

blocks.html: Count each thing once, in any order. Know where you started, and stop when you get back there.
Rows and circles change how things look, not how many there are. The count stays the same as long as each thing gets exactly one number.

blocks.title: Counting a circle
blocks.q: 12 ducks sit in a circle. How do you count them?
steps: Tap (or put a finger on) one duck. Say 1.
Go around, saying 2, 3, 4 … for each duck.
Stop before you reach the first duck again. The last number was 12.

blocks.name: tenframe
blocks.cap: A ten frame helps with big counts: 14 is a full frame and 4 more.

blocks.html: In a circle, losing track of where you started and counting some twice. Mark the first one, by tapping it or putting a finger on it, before you begin.
For grown-ups: Put 12 to 20 small objects in a circle and ask your child to count them. Watch whether they mark a starting point.
